Article Title: CJP protesters enter gurdwara to evade police detention in Delhi, don cockroach helmets
Article Text:
Police personnel detain Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters

NEW DELHI: Protesters wearing cockroach-antennae helmets, raising slogans and seeking refuge inside a gurdwara to evade detention marked the proposed Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi on Saturday.Delhi Police detained around 500 protesters attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, where the demonstration was scheduled to begin at 10:30 am, after denying permission for the gathering and enforcing prohibitory orders across the area.The demonstration was scheduled to begin at 10.30 am at Jantar Mantar, but police prevented protesters from reaching the site, citing prohibitory orders in the New Delhi area. Police had earlier denied permission for the gathering.According to police sources, protesters were detained from several locations, including near Regal Cinema in Connaught Place, Minto Bridge and Akashwani Bhawan. Drones were deployed to monitor movement, while personnel guarded key intersections and roads leading to Jantar Mantar.As police chased demonstrators attempting to regroup, some reached the area near Shivaji Stadium Metro Station and raised slogans against the police.A group of around 10 to 20 protesters marched along the road, shouting, "Your children will be suffering too".When one protester moved into the middle of the road and raised slogans, police personnel ran towards him to apprehend him. Buses carrying detainees were later seen leaving the area, with some protesters shouting "Inquilab Zindabad" and others displaying their press cards from inside the vehicles. A few protesters also entered a gurdwara amid the police action.Amid the restrictions, Anand, a Delhi resident employed in the private information technology sector, wore a helmet modified to resemble cockroach antennae. Explaining his gesture, he told PTI, "This is my own way of paying a tribute to the CJP and opposition alliance leader because what the current dispensation is doing is not in line with what the government should ideally be doing."He said the heavy security presence was curtailing freedom of expression and people's fundamental rights.Separately, police sources said more than 600 people with criminal records had been detained across all 15 districts as a preventive measure ahead of the proposed demonstration.Special Commissioner of Police (Law & Order) Devesh Srivastava told PTI, "We have made elaborate security arrangements today and areas neighbouring bordering states have been picketed in coordination with neighbouring police force.Senior officers have been deployed. Along with that we are getting cooperation from citizens and our community policing teams like Aman Committee are working."He added, "The situation is under control. People who are going to Jantar Mantar are being detained as we had already said that no permission for such protest is granted."The CJP called the demonstration over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, used for voter registration.
Article Summary: CJP called the demonstration over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police detained around 500 protesters attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, where the demonstration was scheduled to begin at 10:30 am.

Article Title: 'Our Gen Z deserves better than Emer-GenZ': Shashi Tharoor slams 'war-like deployment' of cops for CJP protest
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor criticised the heavy security deployment and restrictions in Delhi ahead of the CJP protest, saying Gen Z deserved better

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Saturday criticised the heavy security deployment across Delhi in the wake of Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest against the Election Commission , describing the arrangements as “war-like” and questioning the restrictions imposed on citizens seeking to demonstrate peacefully.In a post, Tharoor said he had returned to the national capital after 2am and had “rarely seen anything like” the situation unfolding in Delhi, citing checkpoints, concrete barriers, spike strips, the deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary personnel, cancellation of 250 trains and closure of 45 metro stations. He also referred to reports of young people being detained from their homes and streets in and around Delhi.Tharoor criticised the suspension of internet services in central Delhi, calling it the “most regressive (as well as repressive)” measure. He said freedom of movement had been “completely shackled” and pointed out that Jantar Mantar had been designated as a place where citizens could voice dissent in the heart of the capital.“One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection,” he said.Questioning what would happen if protesters returned on Monday, Tharoor said those detained would have to be released. “Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ,” he added.Tharoor argued that a government confident in the fairness of elections should welcome questions about the electoral process rather than respond with heavy security measures. “The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression,” he said.He also said barricades would not restore public faith in the Election Commission and urged the poll body to answer questions raised by citizens. Calling the situation “utterly shameful and unconscionable”, Tharoor said a democracy’s strength was measured by how it treated those who questioned its functioning.Several demonstrators were detained by Delhi Police after gathering at Jantar Mantar amid extensive barricading and heightened security.The CJP had called for a protest over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing security considerations and procedural requirements.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticised the heavy security deployment across Delhi in the wake of Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest against the Election Commission. He described the arrangements as ‘war-like’ and questioned the restrictions imposed on citizens seeking to demonstrate peacefully.

Article Title: 'Nothing can stop India's youth': Chirag Paswan on metro, train curbs ahead of Oct 10 CJP protest
Article Text:
Union Minister Chirag Paswan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said “nothing can stop” India’s youth, as Indian Railways cancelled several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive in Delhi ahead of a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar on October 10 over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief Paswan, a BJP ally and NDA member, also said Indian youth could not be held back, questioning attempts to disrupt their movement. “These are the youth of India—nothing can stop them. To those attempting to spread such misconceptions, I ask: how many trains can anyone really stop? How much connectivity can be blocked? How many roads can be jammed?” Paswan said.Paswan has also sought to distinguish his position on the Election Commission of India (ECI) from an automatic defence of the ruling establishment. Amid the controversy, he had initially said being part of the Union government did not mean he would blindly defend anyone. He stressed that the ECI was an independent constitutional body and called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to present a robust response to the allegations and address public questions to help restore confidence in the poll panel.However, days later, Paswan said he was satisfied with the ECI’s point-by-point clarifications and criticised the Opposition for what he described as “selective criticism”. His remarks marked a shift from calling for the poll panel to address concerns to endorsing its subsequent explanation.According to news agency ANI, Paswan also said on Friday that the Indian youth have the potential to lead the world, “they possess the capacity to show the world the way—just as previous generations have done—and so, nothing can hold them back.”The remarks come as the Railway Board has directed the cancellation at source of Mail and Express trains departing after 2 pm on October 9 and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10. Sources said the decision followed intelligence inputs and traffic advisories warning of severe congestion around the stations.Also Read| Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies Paswan acknowledged that protests were a democratic right but argued that repeated demonstrations and road blockades inconvenienced ordinary citizens.“In a democracy like India, there is certainly scope for protests, and you should by all means protest. However, I want to understand this: if your sole objective is merely to protest, then go ahead—do it today, or even ten days from now. But protests alone will not yield a solution; dialogue will,” he told ANI.He alleged that Opposition parties were using the issue for political purposes and called on them to engage constructively with the Election Commission to address concerns over the electoral-roll revision.“If you have genuine concerns, go to the Election Commission; I am fully confident that the CEC himself would sit down to answer your questions,” Paswan said.The CJP protest is seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed gathering, citing short notice, previous non-compliance with directions, and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the railway restrictions, writing on X, “Shut down the entire country if you are scared of the youth.”Trinamool Congress leader Derek O’Brien also targeted the government over the cancellations of the Howrah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express and Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express.“This is a big win for the youth of India and @Cockroachisback @abhijeet_dipke Bravo! Even before a ball has been bowled, the shit scared government has its knickers in a twist! (sic)” O’Brien posted on X.Meanwhile, Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary M A Baby has approached the Supreme Court challenging the restrictions ahead of the protest, including train cancellations and proposed metro station closures. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal is representing him, according to the party.Delhi Police has also urged the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation to shut 57 stations, while security has been tightened at several Delhi borders. The CJP has separately alleged that its national organisation co-in-charge Deepak Baliyan was placed under house arrest, a claim that could not be independently verified.
Article Summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan says Indian youth can't be held back. Railways cancels several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive in Delhi ahead of a protest. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is protesting alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed gathering.

Article Title: Who will lead CJP protest? Abhijeet Dipke names Ajinkya Shinde in pre-recorded video
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party names Ajinkya Shinde to lead its Jantar Mantar protest after founder Abhijeet Dipke and two associates are detained at Delhi airport. (Abhijeet Dipke, Ajinkya Shinde)

Security tightened across Delhi

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday named its organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde to lead its protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi after founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police at the airport.The party shared a pre-recorded video of Dipke, which he had filmed on Friday night in anticipation of a possible arrest ahead of the proposed October 10 demonstration demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Also read: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka detained from Delhi airport ahead of Jantar Mantar protest "Until Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are in detention, CJP’s Organization In-Charge Ajinkya Shinde will lead this protest at Jantar Mantar. Abhijeet had pre-recorded this video last night in anticipation of a potential arrest."The development came as security was tightened across the national capital ahead of the CJP's proposed protest. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience to residents.Dipke had earlier said he was prepared to face arrest while travelling to Delhi for the protest. He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration.At least 1500 people had been detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act as authorities stepped up security ahead of the planned demonstration.Traffic restrictions came into force at 6 am, with diversions planned at several locations across the city. Police personnel were deployed at barricades and key intersections to check vehicles and monitor movement around the protest site.The Delhi Traffic Police warned of possible disruptions around Connaught Place, Mandi House, Jantar Mantar, Patel Chowk and other major intersections in central Delhi.The affected stretches included the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Tolstoy Marg-Janpath crossing, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk, Gol Dak Khana and Windsor Place.In its communication to CJP, Delhi Police said the party's intimation did not qualify as a duly filed application for permission. Police guidelines require applications for demonstrations at Jantar Mantar to be submitted at least 10 days in advance.Authorities also cited alleged past violations of protest conditions, including demonstrations continuing beyond the stipulated time limits.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) named organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde to lead its protest at Jantar Mantar. Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police at the airport. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience.

Article Title: What’s happening at Jantar Mantar? CJP’s ‘cockroaches’ grounded before anti-SIR showdown
Article Text:
‘Not even Indira Gandhi did this’: CJP founder alleges police boarded flight to detain leaders

CJP leaders detained inside aircraft

YouTuber Dhruv Rathee detained ahead of protest

35,000 personnel deployed; internet curbs & traffic restrictions

Liquor shops shut, commercial activity affected

Rahul backs demand for CEC’s removal, but Congress skips protest

CJP appeals for peace amid police restrictions

NEW DELHI: As planned, the ‘cockroaches’ could not make their way to Jantar Mantar, with the detention of key Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders before they could reach the protest site throwing the outfit’s ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ plans into disarray. Delhi’s sweeping security crackdown, which has reportedly led to over 1,500 detentions across the capital, further dampened the expected turnout at the demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International airport from Mumbai.The outfit’s head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also detained.The developments came hours before the outfit’s planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ demonstration demanding the removal of Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protest, proposed by the CJP despite Delhi Police denying permission, was expected to draw around 20,000 participants. However, the detention of key organisers and the extensive security deployment have majorly affected preparations for the demonstration.In a video shared on social media, Dipke could be heard alleging that Delhi Police personnel entered the aircraft shortly after it landed to detain him and his fellow leaders.“So, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane. The entire Delhi Police is getting on the plane. This is the fear of Narendra Modi,” Dipke said.“Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals,” he added.In the same video, CJP leaders Ranka and Das could be heard raising slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and “Inquilab Zindabad”.The group termed the detentions "illegal" and alleged that the police action was aimed at preventing its leaders from reaching Jantar Mantar for the planned demonstration.Almost an hour before the CJP leadership arrived at Delhi airport, the outfit’s supporter and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was reportedly detained by Gurugram Police from his residence in Sector 56.Rathee, who lives abroad, had travelled to participate in the demonstration, according to the information shared by the outfit. His reported detention added to the uncertainty surrounding the protest, which had already triggered heightened security arrangements across Delhi and its adjoining areas.Delhi was placed under an extensive security blanket ahead of the proposed mobilisation. Around 35,000 police personnel were deployed, with Central Police personnel also present in large numbers around Jantar Mantar and other key locations.The security arrangements included CCTV surveillance and body cameras fitted to the uniforms of deployed personnel.A section of Delhi Police was also designated as the “Pink Force”.Mobile internet services were scheduled to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar. Authorities also imposed traffic restrictions on roads along Delhi’s borders with Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, as well as routes leading to Jantar Mantar and other parts of New Delhi.Police were coordinating with cab aggregators to regulate vehicle movement, while several trains were reportedly cancelled. The measures formed part of the broader security plan to manage the expected crowds and prevent disruptions across the capital.The scale of the deployment, however, came amid allegations by the CJP that detaining its organisers before they could reach the venue was an attempt to prevent a peaceful protest.The restrictions extended beyond security and transport. Liquor outlets across Delhi were ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10.Commercial activity was also expected to be affected in parts of the city, particularly around Connaught Place. Market associations in Connaught Place, Sadar Bazar and parts of Karol Bagh and Chandni Chowk confirmed closures for October 10.Markets in Green Park, Sarojini Nagar and Greater Kailash, however, were expected to remain open.The curbs and closures added to the disruption surrounding the proposed demonstration, with authorities preparing for a large turnout even as the detention of key organisers cast doubt on the protest’s eventual scale.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his demand for Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, echoing the central demand of the CJP and other opposition voices opposing the SIR exercise.In a post on X, the former Congress chief wrote: "Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. ""Then the repair of democracy will begin," he added, ending his post with the national flag emoji.However, the Congress stayed away from the CJP’s planned demonstration. Rahul travelled to Chennai to attend an event involving his ally and Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay.Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal , meanwhile, had promised to attend the protest with his family. But the detention of key CJP leaders and the heavy security deployment threatened to reduce the gathering well below the turnout initially anticipated by organisers.Kejriwal criticised the Narendra Modi-led Centre over the restrictions, saying: “This is worse than the Emergency, we are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi.”On the day of its planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest, the CJP issued an appeal urging participants to maintain peace, avoid violence and vandalism, follow lawful instructions and ensure that emergency services were not obstructed.The outfit also called on participants to remain peaceful, alert and united. It described the demonstration as an effort to seek accountability over the Election Commission’s special intensive revision of electoral rolls.Despite Delhi Police denying permission for the protest, the CJP had called for a large mobilisation at Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International airport from Mumbai. The outfit’s head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also detained. Around 35,000 police personnel were deployed, with Central Police personnel also present in large numbers around Jantar Mantar and other key locations. Mobile internet services were scheduled to be suspended within a 4-km radius of the protest site.

Article Title: Detained! How CJP demonstration is being curtailed even before it started
Article Text:
Over 1,600 detained

CJP, student leaders condemn detentions

NEW DELHI: Hours before the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned demonstration could begin on Saturday, police action against its leaders and supporters was already under way, with multiple detentions across Delhi and beyond.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das and party leader Ashutosh Ranka were detained from inside the flight after the Mumbai flight landed.Dhruv Rathee was also detained at his Gurugram residence, while CJP legal team head Ratna Singh alleged that she and three other lawyers had been detained ahead of the protest.Police also detained people attempting to reach the Jantar Mantar, with reports of action near Janpath and other parts of the capital.Over 1600 people have been detained across Delhi as a preventive measure ahead of the CJP protest, as authorities stepped up security and moved to prevent the gathering from taking place.More than 400 members of the Students' Federation of India (SFI) were detained in Delhi on Saturday after they began marching towards Jantar Mantar around 10 am, SFI national president Adarsh M Saji told PTI.SFI also alleged that police personnel visited HKS Surjeet Bhawan on Friday night to search for people planning to attend the protest.The building houses the SFI Central Executive Committee office.Several lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were also detained on Bhagwan Das Road after being stopped at police barricades. The protesters raised slogans and carried posters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. A lawyer said police had allowed them to march for around 100 yards before stopping them.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and CPI(M) MP John Brittas were also detained by police following a protest outside Kerala Bhawan in New Delhi.CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby, senior party leader Brinda Karat and other CPI(M) leaders were also detained at Jantar Mantar amid the police action against protesters.Separately, Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, was detained ahead of a protest in Mumbai in support of the CJP's agitation at Jantar Mantar, extending the demonstrations and police action beyond the national capital.The crackdown also extended beyond the national capital, with people travelling to Delhi for the demonstration reportedly intercepted at railway stations in Madhya Pradesh.At least 14 students travelling from Pune were detained at Itarsi after being taken off the Goa Express on Friday.Four CJP volunteers from Telangana had also been detained at Bhopal railway station on October 8 while travelling to Delhi for the protest.The demonstration was called by CJP to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Delhi Police had denied permission for the proposed gathering, citing security and procedural concerns.The detentions and restrictions on movement have raised questions about the extent of preventive police action ahead of a planned demonstration.The exact number of CJP supporters detained across Delhi and other states remains unclear, with reported figures covering different locations and categories of people.CJP condemned the detentions, calling them an attempt to prevent its leaders from joining the protest. Founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the police action at Delhi airport, calling it “dictatorship” after he and two other party leaders were detained.CJP co-convenor Saurav Das also hit back, saying, “Not few. A storm is coming,” in response to reports of protesters being stopped ahead of the demonstration. The party demanded the release of those detained and said the movement would continue.AISA president Neha Bora accused the authorities of undermining democratic values amid the detentions ahead of the CJP protest. “We have shown the world that a dictator hides behind the mask of democracy,” she said, criticising the police action against protesters.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das and party leader Ashutosh Ranka detained from inside the flight after the Mumbai flight landed. Police also detained people attempting to reach the Jantar Mantar, with reports of action near Janpath and other parts of Delhi.

Article Title: Supreme Court asks authorities to release lawyers detained over CJP protest
Article Text:
CJI intervenes over detention of lawyers ahead of CJP protest

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has urged Chief Justice of India to intervene in the detention of lawyers by Delhi Police and central forces, condemning the alleged use of excessive force against advocates protesting peacefully in the Supreme Court area.The association expressed particular concern over the detention of senior and young lawyers, including women advocates, and called for action on the matter.The CJI is understood to have communicated to the authorities to release the detained lawyers."The Supreme Court Bar Association resolves to request the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India to intervene urgently and take up the matter with the concerned authorities so that the whereabouts and safety of every detained advocate are ascertained, they are given access to legal assistance, and those against whom there are no lawful grounds for detention are released immediately. The circumstances of the detentions and the reported use of force be examined, and appropriate action be taken in accordance with law. A copy of this resolution shall be placed before the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India for urgent consideration," the statement by the Association read.Several lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s proposed protest.The advocates, dressed in formal suits, raised slogans and carried posters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation before police stopped them at barricades on Bhagwan Das Road near the Supreme Court.The detentions came amid heightened security across the national capital ahead of the proposed demonstration. Around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi, while entry and exit restrictions remain in place at 45 metro stations.Surveillance has also been stepped up at the city’s borders, railway stations, bus terminals and other sensitive locations.Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest, citing inadequate notice and concerns over compliance with conditions during an earlier demonstration.On Saturday, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in the national capital. Around 1,500 people have been detained so far in connection with the planned protest.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) condemns alleged use of excessive force. CJI understood to have communicated to the authorities to release the detained lawyers. Lawyers marching from Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police.

Article Title: ‘I’m here to get arrested’: CJP chief Dipke’s prediction comes true at Delhi airport
Article Text:
CJP chief Dipke predicted his detention at Delhi Airport

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police at the Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday, ahead of the party’s proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.As he was getting detained, Dipke said, “Even Indra Gandhi didn't do this,” adding that “arrest hone liye hi aaya hu.”Dipke had predicted his arrest, having earlier said that he was prepared to face detention as he was heading to Delhi for the October 10 protest.Accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration, he had said he would not be deterred from fighting for free and fair elections."I wonder why the Prime Minister of this country is so afraid of the nation's youth and its people. What was the need to shut down all railway services? What was the need to halt all metro operations? They have cut off the internet and blocked the roads. They have brought the Army from J&K and deployed it in Delhi. They have summoned CRPF forces from Naxal-affected areas and deployed them in Delhi. Do Narendra Modi and Amit Shah want to wage war against the people of their own country? Is Gyanesh Kumar so dear to them that they would unleash their police and army forces upon their own citizens?"Dipke alleged that the government feared a public backlash and was taking steps to discourage people from joining the protest."PM Modi is afraid; he fears that the people of this country will not vote for him after this. That is why, simply to cling to power, they are picking people up from trains. Announcements are being made in societies warning people not to join the protests. The Delhi Police is visiting homes, telling people not to participate in protests. But why shouldn't we? Protesting is our fundamental right. Article 19 grants us the fundamental right to protest in a democratic and peaceful manner, and that is exactly what we intend to do. "When asked whether he expected to be arrested upon reaching Delhi airport, Dipke said he was ready to face any action and would continue the fight for electoral reforms."If they want to detain or arrest me, let them go ahead. I am ready for it; let them arrest or detain me. It makes no difference to me. Invoke the UAPA, invoke the NSA—go ahead and do it. But we will keep fighting for free and fair elections and to save this country's democracy."Several CJP leaders and content creators were detained on Saturday ahead of the party’s planned protest in the national capital. Security forces detained multiple demonstrators at Dhaula Kuan, while intensive vehicle checks and multi-agency deployments were reported at key entry points to prevent protesters from reaching the designated site.The CJP also shared a video of its legal head, Ratna Singh, who claimed she was being detained while attempting to leave her home in her car. The party further claimed that content creator Dhruv Rathee had been detained.At least 1,100 people have been detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act as security was tightened across the national capital.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police at the Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday. Dipke had predicted his arrest, having earlier said that he was prepared to face detention as he was heading to Delhi.

Article Title: Woman shot dead in Manipur's Kamjong, Kuki-Naga firing continues; curbs imposed
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A woman was allegedly shot dead in Manipur ’s Kamjong district, triggering fresh violence and prompting authorities to impose prohibitory orders, officials told news agency PTI on Saturday.The incident took place around 9.35pm on Friday in Chassad village, a Kuki-majority settlement in the Naga-dominated district, they said.The woman, a mother of five, sustained gunshot wounds near her neck and died within minutes, officials added.The killing led to an exchange of fire between Kuki and Naga armed groups, with the firing continuing on Saturday morning, they said.
Article Summary: The incident took place around 9.35pm on Friday in Chassad village. The woman, a mother of five, sustained gunshot wounds near her neck and died within minutes. The killing led to an exchange of fire between Kuki and Naga armed groups.

Article Title: 'Jantar Mantar will spring up everywhere': Akhilesh warns BJP as 'the nation unites in Delhi'
Article Text:
Akhilesh warns BJP as 'the nation unites in Delhi'

Massive security deployment ahead of ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’

CJP's earlier protest over NEET paper leak

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday backed the Gen Z-led protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, which is demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Akhilesh said the government's attempts to restrict public dissent in the national capital ahead of the high-stakes demonstration would only prove to be a bigger mistake.In a post on X, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister asserted that young people would unite in Delhi despite any obstacles put up by the Centre."It won't stop for anyone's obstruction. Now, the nation will unite in Delhi! We stand with the youthful energy of the nation. If the BJP government thinks it can halt the people through the might of power, this will prove to be an even greater mistake on its part. ‘Jantar-Mantar’ is no longer just a place's name; it has become a symbol of a new consciousness and awakening. If the government stops the protesters, then Jantar-Mantar will spring up everywhere in the country," he said.However, the Congress, an ally of the Samajwadi Party, is not joining the protest. Other opposition parties, including the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Left parties, have extended their support to the Gen Z movement against Gyanesh Kumar and are expected to join the demonstration.Organised by the CJP, the ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest seeks accountability over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The planned demonstration has prompted extensive security arrangements across Delhi, including movement restrictions, a temporary suspension of mobile internet services and detentions. Several student organisations and political groups are also expected to participate.Early on Saturday, a few protesters were detained near Janpath in the Connaught Place area.More than 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the national capital ahead of the protest. The Union home secretary has also directed states and Union Territories to ensure that law and order is maintained.Mobile internet services will remain temporarily suspended within a four-kilometre radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing from 10pm on Friday to 10pm on Saturday, following authorisation from the Union home secretary, according to an official order.The suspension comes amid heightened security preparations for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10.The proposed demonstration follows a protest led by the CJP at Jantar Mantar in June-July this year. The earlier agitation demanded the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister over the NEET paper leak fiasco.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav backs Gen Z-led protest at Jantar Mantar. Demonstration is demanding resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. More than 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed across national capital ahead of protest.

Article Title: ‘Obvious weakness’: Zelenskyy slams Trump’s Russian diesel deal, warns it could prolong war
Article Text:
Zelenskyy calls Russia sanctions relief without de-escalation deal ‘obvious weakness’

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday (local time) warned that easing sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement would be an “obvious weakness” that could prolong the war by allowing Moscow to continue selling petroleum products.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said peace could not be achieved through weakness and called for stronger sanctions, continued support for Ukraine and sustained pressure on Moscow to end the war."Peace never comes through weakness. Today, representatives of the US Congress were in Kyiv – a bipartisan delegation – and I am grateful to them for visiting Ukraine at such a difficult time. They asked: what is needed to end the war? The answer must be strong. There must be sanctions under the Lindsey Graham bill, there must be support for Ukraine in protecting lives, and there must be pressure on Russia for its war. And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different," he wrote.Referring to the diesel announcement, Zelenskyy said, “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world.Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.""Recently, there was a European decision to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs. Since then, Russian strikes and the torment of people have only increased," he added.Citing recent Russian attacks across Ukraine, Zelenskyy said, "This past week alone, there was a brutal Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, aerial bombs were dropped on Kramatorsk – on ordinary city buses – and there have been constant attacks on Kyiv’s energy infrastructure and on the life-sustaining infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa, and our other cities. Dozens of people have been killed and hundreds wounded. "He alleged that Russia was resorting to such attacks because it was struggling to achieve its objectives on the battlefield. "The Russians are compensating for their inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield with this kind of terror. This year, Russia is weaker on the battlefield than at any other point in the war. That is why Putin is relying on terror. That is why he is relying on attempts to strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war," he further said.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was prepared to take reciprocal steps towards de-escalation, adding that the American team was aware of Kyiv’s position."Ukraine is ready to take symmetrical de-escalatory steps, and the American team knows our position. Our strikes on Russian oil refineries and other oil facilities are a response to Russia’s years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine’s energy sector. Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure. This is the kind of agreement we are proposing to America, and we believe the United States has enough power to achieve such a compromise," he said.Zelenskyy’s remarks came after US President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and announced a deal to secure diesel supplies from Russia, marking a shift in Washington’s pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine as the US seeks to address rising fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.In a social media post on Friday, Trump said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. He added that Russia would deliver another 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time”.The announcement came just a month after Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law aimed at curbing Moscow’s oil and gas revenues, which help fund its war against Ukraine.
Article Summary: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said easing sanctions against Russia without a de-escalation deal would be an ‘obvious weakness’ He called for stronger sanctions, continued support for Ukraine and sustained pressure on Moscow to end the war. His remarks came after US President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Article Title: Before CJP protest, Delhi bandh: Mobile net, metro, roads blocked in heart of city

NEW DELHI: Checks at Delhi’s borders and barricaded roads inside, mobile internet snapped and metro stations shut — Delhi Police has put in place stringent measures to stop protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning. Central Delhi looked like an impregnable fortress by Friday night.The fortified city is expected to see around 35,000 security personnel, including those from Delhi Police and paramilitary forces, to stop what the authorities estimate will be a crowd of 20,000 from reaching Jantar Mantar. The protest is scheduled to start at 10am. Police sources said extra forces were requested because the gathering during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in June-July had been “underestimated”.Mobile internet services in a 4km radius from the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing were snapped at 10pm on Friday. The curbs will continue till 10pm on Saturday. Entry and exit at 57 metro stations (later reduced to 45) were stopped till further notice, after Delhi Police’s Transport Range wrote to Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, citing the possibility of “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”.Apart from this, more than 30 blockade points — including some at the borders — have been identified.“Those attempting to create anarchy or move towards the protest site will be detained immediately. The plan is to stop them at the city’s borders,” an officer said.Joint CP Nupur Prasad said CJP submitted its request to hold a protest on Saturday at “very short notice” and hence permission could not be granted. The application was received on Oct 7. “As per the prescribed guidelines, such applications must be submitted at least 10 days before the protest,” she said.Referring to the June-July protests, JCP Nupur Prasad said, “On an earlier occasion, when CJP was granted permission to hold a protest, they failed to follow lawful directions and adhere to the undertakings they had submitted. Consequently, in view of their failure to comply with legal directions and undertakings, and considering the current requirements for maintaining public safety, law and order and traffic regulations, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar has been denied. ”CJP co-convener Saurav Das, however, said the police had known about the protest since Oct 2 when they had announced it. The 10-day timeline is to ensure that adequate security forces are deployed and traffic arrangements are made, he said, pointing out that even before Oct 2, forces had been deployed as other outfits were protesting on the same issue.“This shows that all of this is an excuse. And we vehemently disagree with the very concept of seeking ‘permission’ from govt to protest against it. It’s absurd and doesn’t make any sense. It’s a colonial mindset,” he said.Personnel at some entry points have been asking motorists about their destinations to keep a check on any movement towards central Delhi.Joint Commissioner of Police (Northern Range) Madhur Verma posted on X Friday: “Prepare for the storm. Practise restraint. Protect the peace. Because the true strength of the police is not merely in controlling a crowd, but in doing so with discipline, dignity and minimum force.”Delhi Police also posted an open letter to citizens on X Friday, invoking duty and humanity, asking people to remember that police personnel have families too.An AI-generated image of a postcard appeared with the message: “Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki suraksha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska apna parivar hai, apne log hain. Faraq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi (Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is a person who has a family and own people. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).”In a detailed note, Delhi Police justified the curbs put in place: “The right to peaceful protest is an important democratic right. At the same time, New Delhi houses important establishments and offices of constitutional authorities and the safety and convenience of residents, workers, commuters and businesses must also be protected.Delhi Police is responsible for safeguarding all these interests while maintaining public order,” it said.“The circumstances surrounding the protests held at Jantar Mantar in July must be taken into consideration. Permission had reportedly been granted for a one-day protest, but the gathering continued for approximately a month. During this period, more than 200 police personnel were injured and over 2,000 individuals with criminal antecedents reportedly participated in the protests, contributing to incidents of violence. As the situation escalated, clashes occurred, resulting in injuries to innocent students as well,” it added.
Article Summary: Police sources say extra forces were requested because the gathering during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in June-July had been “underestimated” Mobile internet services in a 4km radius from the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing were snapped at 10pm on Friday. Entry and exit at 57 metro stations (later reduced to 45) were stopped till further notice.

Article Title: JNU sexual harassment claims: BJP questions Rahul Gandhi’s silence

BJP spokesperson Smriti Irani took a strong stance against Rahul Gandhi for failing to address the dismissal of Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from JNU, who faced serious sexual harassment allegations from female students. (Pic Credit: ANI)

The BJP on Friday criticised Rahul Gandhi over his “deafening silence” following Jawaharlal Nehru University’s (JNU) dismissal of Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam over sexual harassment allegations, claiming that it exposed the “hollowness” of the Congress leader’s “smash the patriarchy” slogan.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, party national general secretary Smriti Irani said Gandhi’s silence on the matter demonstrated that the legal framework, rather than the Gandhi family, safeguards the rights and safety of Indian women.She also criticised Gandhi over his exchange of posts with Elon Musk amid a controversy surrounding Starlink’s satellite internet services in India.JNU on Friday dismissed Akoijam from service with immediate effect after an inquiry into sexual harassment allegations against him found him guilty. Article Summary: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam was dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University over sexual harassment allegations. Police cite legal position on unauthorised protests

NEW DELHI: Delhi police has justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, citing past violence, alleged assaults on women constables and the need to maintain public safety. The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary to prevent overcrowding and keep the capital functioning.In a statement posted on X, the force said, "The right to protest must be protected, but so must the right of a city to function safely. Responsible policing is about balancing both."The police cited violence during a protest in July to explain its concerns.According to the statement, permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration, but it continued for a month. More than 200 police personnel were injured, while over 2,000 people with criminal antecedents joined the protest, contributing to the violence.The police said the situation eventually spiralled out of control, leading to clashes in which students were also injured. It added that women constables had been molested and assaulted by protesters at Jantar Mantar in the past week.The police also pointed to the limited capacity of Jantar Mantar, saying the site could accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. It said restrictions were needed to prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area.The force said Delhi Police had to balance the right to protest with the safety of residents and the capital's economic interests. It added that the city could not be brought to a halt every time a demonstration took place.According to the statement, seeking permission allows authorities to estimate crowd numbers and plan traffic diversions, emergency access and safe movement around the protest site. The police said this would help demonstrators raise their concerns while allowing residents, workers and businesses to continue with their daily activities.The police said the Cockroach Janta Party was proceeding with its planned gathering without permission. Citing the Supreme Court's position, the statement said a protest held without permission was unlawful and participants could face prosecution.It added that organisers were responsible for explaining the legal position to those they invited to attend."The restrictions being put in place today are temporary. They are intended to regulate the flow of people, prevent overcrowding and keep protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area safe," the statement read.The police said the precautions were intended to ensure that people could raise their concerns peacefully without compromising public safety or disrupting the functioning of the city.

The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary.
